hazards.reason: Product.items changes from a list of INTEGER to a list of REAL: SQLite converts each element with a cast that never fails, so the conversion does not keep every element: an integer past 2^53 is rounded.
hazards.subject: table/product/column/items

hazards.reason: Copying product holds the database's write lock for time that grows with the table.
hazards.subject: table/product

hazards.reason: Product.items changes from a list of INTEGER to a list of REAL: servers built from the previous version still read and write a list of INTEGER.
hazards.subject: table/product/column/items

hazards.reason: SQLite's ALTER TABLE cannot convert the elements of items, so the step rebuilds product: it copies the rows into a new table, drops the old one and renames the new one, with foreign keys off.
hazards.subject: table/product

statements:
CREATE TABLE "_new_product" (
  "id" TEXT DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(4)) || '-' || hex(randomblob(2)) || '-4' || substr(hex(randomblob(2)), 2) || '-' || substr('89ab', 1 + (random() & 3), 1) || substr(hex(randomblob(2)), 2) || '-' || hex(randomblob(6)))) NOT NULL,
  "title" TEXT NOT NULL,
  "price" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  "items" TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY ("id")
)

INSERT INTO "_new_product" ("id", "title", "price", "items")
SELECT "id", "title", "price", CASE WHEN "product"."items" IS NOT NULL THEN (SELECT json_group_array(CAST("_element"."value" AS REAL) ORDER BY "_element"."key") FROM json_each("product"."items") AS "_element") END
FROM "product"
steps.subject: table/product
